title: Follow through and target identification
subtitle: Finishing the shot, and knowing where the bullet stops

lines: This episode covers follow through, the important points to remember, and target identification.
The book says that to be classified as a competent shooter, you must be consistent.

scenes.definition: Continuing to do, for two or three seconds, everything you did before the gun fired.
lines: Follow through means that you will continue to do, for two or three seconds, everything that you did before the gun fired.
The idea of follow through is to prevent sudden relaxation or movement that will affect accuracy.

scenes.heading: Master all the fundamentals
lines: To be classified as a competent shooter, you must be consistent.
And in order to be consistent, you must master all the fundamentals of shooting.

lines.text: As a reminder, they are stance, grip, trigger squeeze and breathing.
Then sight alignment, sight picture, and follow through.

scenes.heading: Important points to remember
bullets: Trigger finger not too far through the guard
Don't jerk: even pressure, beginning to end
Same grip and trigger position every shot
lines: The book lists four important points to remember.

lines.text: One: do not insert your trigger finger too far through the trigger guard.

lines: This will cause you to pull the firearm off to one side.

lines.text: Two: do not jerk the trigger.

lines: Squeeze the trigger with an even amount of pressure from beginning to end.

lines.text: Three: maintain the same grip and trigger position for every shot.
Four: squeeze the trigger smoothly, but positively.

rule.text: Before firing the gun the target should always be identified.

lines: Now, target identification.
Before firing the gun, the target should always be identified.
Take into consideration not only where the bullet will initially strike, but also where that bullet will ultimately come to rest.

rule.text: Remember that you are liable for where that bullet stops.

lines: If you are in a life threatening situation and need to fire your gun in a built-up area or public place, remember this.
You are liable for where that bullet stops.

scenes.heading: Unsafe angle
scenes.caption: Unsafe angle: open space behind the attacker
lines: Here we see an unsafe angle.
Shooting from this angle will endanger innocent bystanders behind the attacker.

scenes.heading: Correct angle
scenes.caption: Correct angle: a safe backstop behind the attacker
lines: Here the shooter has moved to the right, in order to secure a safe backstop behind the attacker.
There is still the possibility of the bullet ricocheting off the wall to the right.
But much of the energy of that bullet will have been removed by the wall.
So it should not cause a fatal injury after the ricochet.

scenes.heading: Where will the bullet stop?
bullets: Where will the bullet come to rest?
The body is seldom capable of stopping a bullet
It can endanger bystanders behind your attacker

lines.text: Don't only take into account whether or not you are able to hit the target.
Also consider where the bullet will come to rest.
Bear in mind that the human body is seldom capable of stopping a bullet.
So it is highly likely the bullet will pass through your attacker, and can endanger innocent bystanders behind your attacker.

scenes.heading: Low light and darkness
bullets: Never fire at a target you can't properly identify
Positively identify the target, in any situation

lines.text: When faced with low light or darkness, never fire at a target that cannot be properly identified.
In other words, do not shoot at shadows.
In any situation, a target must be positively identified, in order for you to align your sights correctly.

lines: That means, be sure about what you are shooting at.

rule.text: Random shooting in the general direction of your intended target is not permitted by Law.

lines: Random shooting in the general direction of your intended target is not permitted by Law.
And positive target identification will also increase your accuracy when shooting.
